\section{Gaussian Space --- Rotation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Rotation
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Rotation: Introduction}
Gaussian rotations preserve the joint Gaussian law. Their disagreement probabilities satisfy continuity, subadditivity, and equal-step lower bounds.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Rotation: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Rotation invariance of paired Gaussian vectors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $t\in\mathbb R$. The planar rotation by $t$, applied
coordinatewise to a pair of vectors in $\mathbb R^n$, preserves the product of two
standard Gaussian measures on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subadditivity of rotation sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_subadditive}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}

  {pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p016-b001}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $s,t\in\mathbb R$. The
rotation sensitivity of $A$ at angle $s+t$ is at most the sum of its rotation
sensitivities at angles $s$ and $t$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, let $\ell\ge 0$ be an integer,
and let $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_\ell\in\mathbb R$. The rotation sensitivity of $A$ at
angle $\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\delta_j$ is at most $\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}s_A(\delta_j)$, where
$s_A(u)$ denotes the rotation sensitivity at angle $u$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, let
$\delta\in\mathbb R$, and let $\ell$ be a positive natural number. Then the Gaussian
rotation sensitivity satisfies $$s_A(\delta)\le \ell\,s_A(\delta/\ell).$$
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. The rotation sensitivity of
$A$ at angle $\pi/2$ is $2\gamma_n(A)\bigl(1-\gamma_n(A)\bigr)$, where $\gamma_n$ is
standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable with $\gamma_n(A)=1/2$, then $s_A(\pi/(2\ell))\ge1/(2\ell)$ for every positive integer $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of rotation sensitivity at zero]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_tendsto_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. The rotation sensitivity of
$A$ tends to $0$ as the real angle tends to $0$.
\end{lemma}
